findings.evidence: New reviewers listed are "intent-completeness, spec-completeness, architecture-conformance, security code reviewer", plus the existing requirements auditor and security architect. KIT-DESIGN.md stage 4 and WORKFLOW.md S4 also require an "LLM: workflow/IaC reviewer + zizmor, actionlint, Trivy" when .github/ or infra/ change. The intent removes the CI reviewer jobs in security.yml but never says where workflow/IaC review runs after that.
findings.recommendation: Add the workflow/IaC reviewer to the local reviewer set, either as a new agent or as the existing one run locally, and name zizmor/actionlint/Trivy among the path-scoped CI scanners. If it is deliberately deferred, list it under Out of scope.

findings.evidence: The Functional section takes on all checks "as in WORKFLOW.md" for intent, spec, plan and code, including the template-structure script, the plan SR/mitigation ID cross-check, the named-test-exists check, the plan-drift check and the path-scoped scanners. No success criterion covers any of these. The criteria cover only the report hash/verifier, SR escalation, comments, $0 spend and usage.
findings.recommendation: Add one testable criterion per script check, e.g. "a PR that changes a file not listed in plan.md fails CI", "a plan missing a task for an SR in the traceability file fails the cross-check", "an intent.md with an empty required section fails the structure check", "a docs-only PR runs only gitleaks + verifier".

findings.evidence: Criterion 6: "One full stage ... completes within the owner's Pro plan usage window". It is not defined what counts as passing (no usage-limit message? a share of the 5-hour window? which stage, since code and spec costs differ?). KIT-DESIGN lists this as "Open: Pro plan usage limits ... (verify against real usage)".
findings.recommendation: Owner to state the pass threshold, e.g. "the heaviest stage of 0001 (code) finishes without hitting a Pro usage limit message", and what happens if it fails (accept, or reduce reviewers/rounds).

findings.evidence: Review reports are classed "Personal/sensitive? no" and kept in "git history (public repo)". Reports hold SR findings (e.g. open violations like SR-004 in touched code), and these become public before any fix. That includes open/needs-human findings committed at PR time.
findings.recommendation: Owner to confirm that publishing unfixed security findings in a public repo is acceptable. Otherwise state a rule for them (e.g. SR findings are summarised by ID only, or the details go to a private location) and update the sensitivity column.

findings.evidence: "Any finding against a security requirement escalates to the owner". KIT-DESIGN adds the owner's options: fix, or accept the risk as a reviewed exception (SR, reason, expiry) in appsec-baseline exceptions/, "which the gate reads; the re-run then passes". The intent does not say whether the exception file format and the gate reading exceptions/ are part of 0001. It also does not say how an owner decision is recorded in the PR (finding status accepted-risk).
findings.recommendation: State whether the exceptions/ mechanism and the finding statuses (fixed/open/needs-human/accepted-risk/carried) are in scope for 0001, or list them under Out of scope.

findings.evidence: The security-tester job in deploy.yml is removed, and the release-time ZAP → SR mapping and deploy stop are deferred to 0002. The intent does not say what the release path does between 0001 and 0002: does the existing ZAP baseline/smoke test keep running unchanged, and does anything still stop a deploy?
findings.recommendation: Add one line describing interim release behaviour (e.g. "deploy.yml keeps ZAP baseline + smoke test as today; no gate on alerts until 0002").

findings.evidence: KIT-DESIGN step 6 has the CI verifier check that hashes match "and whose verdict allows", plus a template structure check. The intent's CI bullet mentions only "exists and matches the PR's files".
findings.recommendation: Add "and its verdict allows" and the template-structure check to the CI bullet so the spec does not have to infer them.

findings.evidence: "`/stage <stage> <id>`, later \"next stage\"". It is unclear whether the "next stage" trigger is part of 0001. The optional git-push hook backstop from KIT-DESIGN is also not mentioned either way.
findings.recommendation: Say whether "next stage" and the push-blocking hook are in scope; if not, add them to Out of scope.

findings.evidence: The change removes workflows under .github/ and edits lab-admin settings (required checks, repo variables, labels, Actions allowlist). dogs-app CLAUDE.md forbids agents from editing .github/ (hook + CODEOWNERS), and lab-admin is a separate repo. The intent does not say who makes these edits in the code stage, or how plan drift / the verifier treat cross-repo changes.
findings.recommendation: State that the .github/ edits and the lab-admin PR are made by the owner (or an exempted path), and whether the lab-admin change is part of this change's code stage or a follow-up PR.

findings.evidence: Criterion 1 measures $0 spend only for "idea to a merged intent PR", while the change covers intent through code. Criterion 2 covers dogs-app workflows but not removal of the lab-admin required checks/variables/labels/allowlist entries.
findings.recommendation: Extend criterion 1 to all four stages of a change (or of 0001 itself). Add a check that the lab-admin required-check list, variables, labels and allowlist no longer reference the removed LLM jobs.
